lines.opener: *a squalid old man leans on a pole in a leaking boat and holds out a filthy palm* Fare. One obol. Lethe plain, Donkey-shearings, Taenarum... I've had six of your leftovers this week, passenger, and not one of them paid.
lines.openerHostile: *he levels his barge-pole at you like a spear* Another fare-dodger. I can always tell. Get off my bank.
lines.like: *a grunt, almost approving* ...Hm. That's more like it.
lines.dislike: *he spits into the river* Don't start. Just don't.
lines.hate: *the barge-pole swings round at your head* FARE-DODGER! Nobody crosses free!
lines.flirt: *a long, flat stare* The fare is still one obol, passenger.
lines.join: *he looks at his boat, then at you, and sighs* Somebody else can pole the dead across for a while. I'm owed a holiday. I'll come along.
lines.demand: *the palm comes out again* Fare. Obol, or two hundred in gold. Prices have gone up.
lines.gift: *he fishes a little coin out of his beard and flicks it to you* Here. You'll need it someday. Don't lose it.
lines.thanks: *he bites the coin, then pockets it* Good. Proper fare. Rare these days.
lines.letPass: *he pushes off from the bank* Go on, then. I'll see you again. Everybody sees me again.
lines.neutral: *he leans on his pole and bails a little water out of the boat*
lines.ai: *he squints at you* A-I? Is that some new kind of dead? Do they pay?
lines.refuseJoin: Ha! Ask me to leave the boat? Who'd row the dead across, you?
lines.leaveNow: *he pushes off into the mist* Next! Who's for the Lethe plain?
